newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia replaces "stressed out" riot officer.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia replaces "stressed out" riot officer.

text.p: An Indonesian army officer commanding the district where a Moslem mob rioted in October has been replaced because he is "stressed out", the Jakarta Post newspaper said on Saturday.
Five people died and more than 20 churches were set on fire during the October 10 riots in the worst incident of religious violence in recent years.

The paper quoted Major-General Imam Utomo, the head of the Brawijaya regional military command covering East Java, as saying on Friday that he had replaced Lieutenant-Colonel Imam Prawoto, the chief of the Situbondo military district

Utomo said he had been observing Prawoto since the riots in which 25 Christian churches and one temple were destroyed around Situbondo, about 160 kilometres (100 miles) east of Indonesia's second city of Surabaya.
"Over the past two months, I saw him getting more and more stressed out. He could only think of the 54 suspects and nothing else," Utomo was quoted as telling a media conference.

"Every day, people asked him about the riot. That's why he became stressed out. If this situation went on, the task of safeguarding the general elections next year wouldn't proceed smoothly," he said.
General elections are set for May next year.
Utomo refused to say if his subordinate, who will be transferred to army headquarters in Jakarta, had been replaced as a direct consequence of the riots.
The official Antara news agency reported on Saturday that the first of the trials of the suspects arrested after the riots will begin in two separate court proceedings on Monday.
The report did not say how many would be tried. However, authorities confirmed this week that one of the 54 suspects had died in custody in circumstances still being investigated.
